- Additional whole-slice sweeps: 168 effect_vs_control placebo comparators checked against the same table's placebo cell; every numeric readout_value grepped against the raw source text; controlled vocabulary checked on 10 enum columns; pooled-vs-per-compound attribution checked on all 387; duplicate-locus check on all 387.
summary:
SOURCE RETRIEVED IN FULL. Main text + all 7 tables parsed from the PMC JATS XML (efetch db=pmc id=5467133); supplementary Tables S1-S12 and Supplementary Figs S1-S2 parsed with PyMuPDF from Supp_Data.pdf, and Fig 1 read as an image, both from the Europe PMC supplementaryFiles zip for PMC5467133. Identifiers independently confirmed: PMID 28145801, PMCID PMC5467133, doi 10.1089/nat.2016.0650, Nucleic Acid Ther 27(3), 2017.

METHOD. Rather than eyeballing rows, I transcribed every source cell of Tables 3,4,5,6,7 and Supplementary Tables S2,S4,S5,S6,S7,S8,S9,S11,S12 into an independent machine-readable reference (scratchpad/ref.py) built directly from the parsed XML/PDF, then wrote a checker (scratchpad/verify.py) that parses each row's `source_table` locus string, looks up that exact cell, and compares readout_value, the 'n of N subjects' fraction in notes, the dose band, and thrombocytopenia_grade against the rubric. 377 of 387 rows resolved to a table cell and were checked this way; the remaining 10 (4 Fig 1 rows, 6 body-text rows) were checked by hand against the figure image and the quoted sentences.

VALUE ACCURACY: PERFECT. Zero value errors in 377 auto-checked cells. Every percentage, every n/N pair, every LS mean, every Mantel-Haenszel risk difference and CI, and every baseline mean(SD) matches the printed source. The extractor correctly reproduced the source's awkward multiple-denominator structure - Table 3 panel B uses n=2,363 for the relative-threshold rows but n=2,368 for the absolute-threshold rows, and Supplementary Table S6 uses three different n rows (1,877 / 1,878 / 1,788) - and got every denominator right. It also kept Table 3 (52 trials, incl. open-label) and Supplementary Table S6 (42 RCTs only) as separate populations rather than conflating them, which is the single easiest way to corrupt this article.

CROSS-TABLE CONTAMINATION: NONE. I checked all 168 rows whose effect_vs_control is of the form 'Xpct_vs_Ypct_placebo' and confirmed Y is the placebo cell of THE SAME table, not borrowed from a neighbouring table with a similar-looking value.

GRADING. The two conventions I was asked to stress-test both hold. (1) Incidence rows are graded on EVENT SEVERITY, not incidence size: e.g. TMSR319, the 0.04% incidence of a <75-50 K/uL nadir, is correctly grade 2, not downgraded for rarity; 26 such small-incidence severe-band rows are all graded on the band. (2) Explicit zeros are grade 0: all 206 grade-0 rows carry an EXPLICIT ZERO note and record which grade the band would otherwise have carried, so the severe bands (<50-25, <25, <50 K/uL - 82 rows) remain findable with their denominators intact.

BLEEDING: NOT INFLATED. All 23 bleeding/clinical-outcome rows are graded 0 or 1. No row in the entire slice carries grade 3, which is correct - this source reports no subject below 50 K/uL anywhere, all bleeding mild, and the primary bleeding endpoint LOWER on drug (1.1%) than placebo (1.6%). The extractor explicitly documented resisting the keyword-driven grade-3 inflation the schema warns about.

POOLED vs PER-COMPOUND ATTRIBUTION: CLEAN. Zero class-level aggregates are attributed to a named compound. All 267 rows from the pooled loci (Tables 3 and 5; Supp S2, S4, S5, S6, S7, S8, S9, S12) carry oligo_name "2'-MOE ASO class pool". The 114 mipomersen rows come only from genuinely mipomersen-specific loci (Table 4, Table 6, Table 7, Supp S11, and the longer-term-mipomersen Results paragraphs); the 4 ISIS 104838 rows come only from Fig 1, which the caption states is ISIS 104838; the 2 ISIS 416858 rows come only from the Discussion paragraph naming IONIS-FXIRx. One row I initially flagged, TMSR103, sits under the mipomersen section heading but quotes the sentence 'Assessment of all RCTs found...', so class-pool attribution is right.

FIGURE ROWS: NO FABRICATION. The four Fig 1 rows correctly carry readout_value=TBD and state the figure was not digitized. I opened the figure image and every qualitative claim in their notes checks out: the reference lines really are -30% (top) and LLN + 50K (bottom); the placebo solid line really does stay above baseline for the whole study; the 200 mg/week dashed line really does reach about -30% at week 12; the 400 mg/week dash-dot line really is the steepest with recovery in follow-up; and no group trend line comes near 50 K/uL.

CONTROLLED VOCABULARY: LEGAL. study_type, species, tissue, delivery_method, dose_or_conc_unit, readout_category, effect_direction, redistribution, is_platelet_specific and thrombocytopenia_grade are all within the schema enums for all 387 rows. No duplicate (locus, readout, oligo) triples.

REDISTRIBUTION: CORRECT AND CONSERVATIVE. The article is CC BY-NC (confirmed from the JATS permissions block and the Europe PMC license field 'cc by-nc'). The schema's cc_by class is for Attribution licences only and there is no BY-NC class, so the fallback to summary_stat on all 387 rows is the right call - and notably the extractor did NOT over-claim cc_by for a NonCommercial article.

WHAT I AM CORRECTING (5 rows). The bleeding-family rows share a boilerplate grade rationale asserting 'the mipomersen incidence was not raised above placebo'. That is true for the primary endpoints but FALSE for five cells where mipomersen genuinely exceeds placebo: ecchymosis (0.4 vs 0.0), hematocrit decreased (0.4 vs 0.0), the general/administration-site SOC total (36.4 vs 15.5), injection site hematoma (31.8 vs 14.0) and injection site hemorrhage (6.1 vs 1.6). The grade-1 assignment is still correct - it rests on the source's 'all events were mild' and on non-attribution to thrombocytopenia, and the three injection-site rows are already correctly flagged is_platelet_specific=FALSE as local subcutaneous reactions - but the stated justification is wrong, so I have rewritten the rationale text. Values, grades and all other fields are unchanged.

CAVEATS FOR CONSUMERS, NOT ERRORS. (a) 31 placebo-arm rows carry thrombocytopenia_grade 1 or 2, because the convention grades the band observed in that arm regardless of arm. Every such row discloses the placebo context in notes, so this is internally consistent, but a downstream model joining grade to design features must exclude dose_or_conc_value=='0' or it will learn that the class pool causes grade-2 events at zero dose. (b) The <0.5 x BSLN band (a >50% relative decline with no absolute count implied) is graded 2 on the rubric's 'requiring monitoring' clause; this is a documented judgement call applied uniformly to all 23 such rows and disclosed in every one of them, but it is the one convention in this slice a reviewer could reasonably set to 1 instead. (c) Supplementary Table S8 rows omit the per-comparison subject n from notes (the trial count is present); cosmetic only, values verified.

OVERALL CONFIDENCE: VERY HIGH. This is the cleanest block I could have hoped to attack. I set out to refute it and could not falsify a single readout_value, locus, grade, or attribution. The only defect I could substantiate is a misleading sentence in the notes of 5 rows.
